Trend and cycle analysis in a web browser

Source: R/app.R
mhp_app.Rd

mhp_app() starts the application of mhpfilter: load a series (the example us_macro or a CSV file), filter it with the HP, modified HP or fully modified HP filter, compare the three filters, inspect their weights, gains and end-point loss, filter all the series of a file at once and run the power comparison of Hanif, Iqbal and Choudhary (2017). Every result page shows an interpretation computed from the results (mhp_interpret()), the output as R prints it, formatted tables, plots and the R code that repeats the analysis, each with a Copy button.

Usage

mhp_app(launch.browser = interactive(), ...)

mhp_app_object()

Arguments

launch.browser

passed to shiny::runApp(): TRUE (default in an interactive session) opens the application in the web browser.

...

further arguments to shiny::runApp(), such as port.

Value

mhp_app() is called for its side effect and returns the value of shiny::runApp() when the application is closed; mhp_app_object() returns the application object (for shiny::runApp(), shiny::testServer() or deployment on a server).

Details

The application needs the suggested packages shiny, bslib and DT. Plots are sent to the browser as WebP images when magick is installed (smaller than PNG; PNG otherwise) and can be downloaded as PNG, PDF or WebP. Text is set in IBM Plex Sans and output in IBM Plex Mono when the browser can reach Google Fonts, in the system fonts otherwise.

See also

mhp_filter, fmhp_filter, fmhp_compare, mhp_interpret

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  mhp_app(
      launch.browser = TRUE
    )
}
